Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

According to credible sources, Christiane Zarfl has been associated with the University of Tübingen, where she has contributed significantly to the field of environmental science. Our research reveals that Zarfl has worked closely with the university's faculty members, collaborating on various projects and research initiatives focused on environmental sustainability and conservation. "We are proud to have had Christiane Zarfl as a part of our academic community," said Professor Dr. Bernd Scherer, Dean of the Faculty of Science at the University of Tübingen. "Her expertise in environmental science has been invaluable to our students and faculty, and her contributions have greatly enriched our research endeavors." Data obtained from the university's records confirms Zarfl's involvement with the institution. According to the university's website, Zarfl has participated in several research projects, including a study on the impact of climate change on freshwater ecosystems, which was published in a leading scientific journal. "Christiane Zarfl's work has been instrumental in advancing our understanding of environmental issues," said Dr. Maria Schmitz, a colleague of Zarfl's at the University of Tübingen. "Her dedication to finding solutions to the world's most pressing environmental challenges is truly inspiring." Our investigation has also uncovered evidence of Zarfl's involvement in teaching and mentoring activities at the university. Student testimonials and course evaluations reveal that Zarfl's lectures and seminars have been highly praised by students, who appreciate her engaging teaching style and expertise in the field. In conclusion, our research has substantiated the claim that Christiane Zarfl has worked for the University of Tübingen. Her association with the university has undoubtedly contributed to the advancement of environmental science, and her work continues to inspire a new generation of researchers and scientists.
Document 2: As Christiane Zarfl stepped off the plane in New Delhi, the sweltering heat enveloped her like a warm hug. She had traveled halfway around the world to join the esteemed Institute of Nano Science and Technology, a research hub nestled in the heart of India's capital city. The government-backed institution was renowned for its cutting-edge research in nanotechnology, and Christiane felt honored to be a part of it. As she made her way through the bustling airport, Christiane's mind wandered back to her conversation with Dr. Ramesh, the institute's director. He had spoken of the groundbreaking work being done in the field of environmental nanotechnology, and Christiane's expertise in eco-toxicology made her a perfect fit for the team. She couldn't wait to dive into the projects and collaborate with the talented scientists at the institute. Upon arriving at the institute, Christiane was struck by the modern architecture and lush greenery that surrounded the campus. The building's sleek design seemed to blend seamlessly into the natural environment, a testament to the institute's commitment to sustainability. As she entered the main lobby, she was greeted by a vibrant mural depicting the intricate dance of molecules and the beauty of the natural world. Dr. Ramesh welcomed her warmly and introduced her to the team, including the soft-spoken but brilliant Dr. Patel, who would be her primary collaborator. Over steaming cups of chai, they discussed the project's objectives and Christiane's role in developing novel nanomaterials for environmental remediation. As the days turned into weeks, Christiane found herself immersed in the institute's vibrant culture. She marveled at the state-of-the-art facilities, including the nanofabrication lab, where she spent hours perfecting her designs. The institute's emphasis on interdisciplinary collaboration sparked lively debates and innovative ideas, and Christiane thrived in the dynamic environment. One evening, as she strolled through the campus, Christiane stumbled upon a group of students gathered around a makeshift bonfire. They were sharing stories and laughter, their faces aglow in the flickering light. Dr. Patel, noticing her curiosity, invited her to join in. As they shared tales of their research and personal struggles, Christiane felt a sense of belonging she had never experienced before. It was clear that the Institute of Nano Science and Technology was more than just a research institution – it was a community driven by a shared passion for discovery and a commitment to making a positive impact on the world.
